sections.html:
Probate runs through the Register of Wills in the county where the decedent had a last family or principal residence. That office grants letters, the court-recognized proof that one person may act for the estate. Disputes and sale approvals go to the orphans' court division of the same county.

For a house, letters come first. Without them nobody can sign a deed for the estate, and a title company will not insure a buyer. The rules sit in Title 20 of the Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes, the Probate, Estates and Fiduciaries Code.

sections.h2: Which county's Register of Wills handles the estate?
sections.html:
Section 3151 says letters for a Pennsylvania domiciliary are granted only by the register of the county of the decedent's last family or principal residence. Someone who lived in Erie County and owned a second house elsewhere is still probated in Erie County. If the decedent was domiciled outside Pennsylvania, any county where estate property sits may grant the letters, and those letters then cover the whole Commonwealth.

The petition must be sworn. Section 3153 calls for the decedent's name, age, domicile, last residence and date and place of death, the heirs where there is no will, and the estimated value of personal property plus the estimated value and location of real property in Pennsylvania. The house address will appear on the petition itself.

sections.h2: Who gets letters, and in what order
sections.html:
If the will names an executor, section 3155(a) directs the register to grant letters testamentary to that person, even if the executor has declined a trust under the will. With no will, or no executor who acts, letters of administration go to someone on a priority list.

Priority for letters of administration under 20 Pa.C.S. 3155(b)
OrderPerson
1Those entitled to the residuary estate under the will
2The surviving spouse
3Intestate heirs, with preference by size of share
4Principal creditors of the decedent
5Other fit persons

A person who renounces may name a nominee, at the register's discretion. Section 3155(c) adds a waiting period: letters for creditors and other fit persons cannot issue until 30 days after death unless the higher-ranking persons consent.

sections.h2: Can a house skip probate through the small estate process?
sections.html:
Usually not. The small estate petition in section 3102 leaves real estate out of the $50,000 figure. The court may direct distribution of personal property up to $50,000 in gross value, and owning real estate does not limit that authority. But the process distributes personal property. A house still needs a person with authority to convey it.

Section 3101 offers another shortcut that never reaches real estate: an employer may pay up to $10,000 in wages or benefits to a spouse, child, parent or sibling, in that order of preference, whether or not a representative has been appointed. Neither shortcut replaces letters when the house must be sold.

sections.h2: What the personal representative can do with the house
sections.html:
The representative may take possession of, maintain and administer the decedent's real and personal estate. The one exception is real estate occupied at death by an heir or devisee with the decedent's consent. Under section 3311, the representative collects rents and income until the property is sold or distributed, and makes reasonable expenditures to preserve it. Nothing in that section limits the power to sell real estate an heir or devisee occupies.

The sale powers in section 3351 are broad. Unless the will says otherwise, the representative may sell at public or private sale any real property not specifically devised, and may sell specifically devised property with the devisee's joinder. If the will withholds the power, or a judicial sale effect is advisable, section 3353 calls for an order of the orphans' court division. Section 3357 then passes the decedent's full title to the buyer, discharged from legacy liens and estate debts, provided any required bond was given.

  • No will power to sell: ask the court for a section 3353 order.
  • House specifically left to one person: that person joins the deed.
  • Heir living in the house: the representative can still sell it.

sections.h2: A vacant or burdened house during probate
sections.html:
Keeping the house in shape is the representative's job, because section 3311 treats preservation of estate property as part of the role. The statute allows reasonable expenditures necessary to preserve it. Heirs who live far away often find the first months of probate expensive for exactly this reason.

Section 3312 gives one pressure valve. When property is of no value to the estate, the court may authorize the representative to renounce the right to administer it. A house with debts above its worth can fall into that category, though the court decides, and an attorney should advise before anyone asks.

Real estate taxes keep coming. Under 53 Pa.C.S. 8863, property of a decedent's estate may be assessed in the name of the decedent or the personal representative, so bills may still arrive in the decedent's name. Once letters issue, ask the county assessment office to update the mailing address.

sections.h2: Advertising, filings and payments before distribution
sections.html:
The representative must advertise the grant of letters once a week for three successive weeks, in one newspaper of general circulation near the decedent's residence and in the legal periodical designated by court rule. Section 3162 requires the notice to invite claims and ask debtors to pay. The advertisement starts a clock under section 3532: a representative who distributes at their own risk, without an audit, is free of liability to a claimant unless the claim became known within one year after the first complete advertisement, or later but before distribution.

The inventory is due under section 3301(c) by the date the account is filed or the inheritance tax return is due, whichever is earlier, and any party in interest may demand an earlier filing. Inheritance tax is delinquent nine months after death, with a 5 percent discount if paid within three months.

A cash sale can close as soon as letters exist and the title company is satisfied with the signing authority. The estate skips months of repairs, staging and listing, and stops paying carrying costs on an empty house. The representative still handles the inheritance tax, the advertisement and the accounting.

Bring the letters, the will if there is one, the death certificate and any court order to the title company, and ask which other documents it wants from the Register of Wills. If an heir lives in the house, set a move-out date in writing before the closing.

faqs.q: Do I need probate to sell a house in Pennsylvania?
faqs.a: Yes, in most cases. The small estate process covers personal property only, so a house needs a personal representative holding letters from the Register of Wills.

faqs.q: Which county do I file in?
faqs.a: File in the county where the decedent had a last family or principal residence. Section 3151 allows letters for a Pennsylvania domiciliary only from that county's register.

faqs.q: Can an heir living in the house be forced out for the sale?
faqs.a: The representative's power to sell is not limited because an heir or devisee lives there. Ending the occupancy is a matter for the orphans' court or an attorney, and a written move-out date helps.

faqs.q: How long do creditors have to make a claim?
faqs.a: A representative who distributes at their own risk is protected against claims not known within one year after the first complete advertisement, or later but before distribution. The advertisement runs once a week for three weeks.

faqs.q: What happens if there is no will and no relatives?
faqs.a: Under a change effective January 16, 2026, the estate goes first to an endowed community fund in the decedent's municipality, then the school district, then the county, and only then to the Commonwealth.
